title: **Iran Fuel Crisis Deepens as US Sanctions, War Damage, and Panic Buying Trigger Massive Petrol Queues**
text:
**Iran Fuel Crisis Deepens as US Sanctions, War Damage, and Panic Buying Trigger Massive Petrol Queues**"

"By Iman Keyhanfard"

"**Tehran, August 27, 2026** — Long queues have formed at petrol stations across Tehran and several other Iranian cities as fuel shortages, supply disruptions, and widespread panic among motorists intensify. Drivers are reportedly waiting up to two hours in lines that snake around filling stations, while some pumps have shut down entirely after running out of fuel."

"Panic buying has compounded the supply crunch. Drivers are filling up tanks before they are even half empty, driven by fears of imminent price hikes and quota reductions. State-run *Hamshahri* newspaper reported that much of the recent queueing stems not from actual shortages but from "precautionary demand" fueled by anxiety over future fuel policy. Those fears were stoked after Mohsen Haji-Mirzaei, the president's chief of staff, announced that petrol quotas would be reviewed and that consumers would likely pay higher prices for usage beyond their allocated limits."

"Despite authorities distributing a record 26 million litres of petrol in Tehran on Monday — about 30 per cent above the daily average — queues have only grown longer as demand surges. The National Iranian Oil Refining and Distribution Company has denied any nationwide fuel shortage, but reports from provinces including Kerman, Mashhad, Mazandaran, Gilan, Hormozgan, and Fars indicate similar disruptions."

"The issue carries deep political sensitivity. Past efforts to raise petrol prices — most notably in November 2019 — triggered deadly nationwide protests. With Iran's currency plunging to a new low of 2 million rials to the dollar and year-on-year inflation approaching 90 per cent, any further price hikes could stoke renewed public anger."
